body: Webpack 2 does, number 2/3/4 also exist in Babel too and are also filed over there, I just figured I'd make sure they got tracked here too.
Oh, alright. Thanks for the heads-up :)
Uhg... I'll try to fix those ~~edgecases~~ issues... ;)

@loganfsmyth could you please check if this test case covers all issues above?
https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/master/test/cases/parsing/harmony-export-precedence/index.js

i was wrong above. It covered the third case. However, the third case is illegal. See [the spec about module semantics](http://www.ecma-international.org/ecma-262/6.0/#sec-module-semantics-static-semantics-early-errors) @loganfsmyth. Duplicate entries are not allowed
Seems like that test just needs to have the names of the exports tweaked.

The key problem is what's the point of case 3 compared to case 2?

And the comment of case3 is a little misleading:

> should log `a-foo` since named exports take precedence over indirect exports. Currently it throws because the `export * from` tries to redefine the non-configurable property.

there is no `export * from` in case 3.

> Local exports take precedence over indirect exports

this rule is not what the spec indicates.

You're totally right. I was describing the order of operations defined in http://www.ecma-international.org/ecma-262/7.0/#sec-resolveexport, but that doesn't take into account that duplicate export names are already disallowed in http://www.ecma-international.org/ecma-262/7.0/#sec-module-semantics-static-semantics-early-errors via an early error.

One interesting thing is, when i dig down the problem with babel and typescript, it turns out that they both don't behave as 100% as the spec requires.

see [my sample repo](https://github.com/e-cloud/module-export-override-semantic)
